text.title: Single Page Case Study Generation — Worked Example
text.summary: One complete case-study report for a fintech checkout-latency engagement (named version, drafted 5 and published 12 days after delivery, outcome-first title with the 62 percent number, six slots within their sentence counts, two numbers with baseline, final, delta, window and source system, a verbatim VP quote with an email permission, 310 words and one chart, one UTM-tracked CTA, review due at 90 days) with a note per value, plus a service-first write-up done five months late and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: A backend freelancer finished a three-week engagement for Kestrel Pay on 2026-08-28: p95 checkout latency went from 1,480 ms to 560 ms and checkout abandonment from 18.4 to 14.1 percent, both readable from the Grafana and GA4 exports the freelancer kept. The VP Engineering agreed by email to a named study and to one sentence being quoted. The study goes on the freelancer's site and into the next proposal pack.

example.title: Kestrel Pay checkout latency, named version
example.note: Delivered 2026-08-28, drafted 2026-09-02 (5 days) and published 2026-09-09 (12 days), inside both windows (r-seven-day-draft-fourteen-day-publish). The title leads with the outcome, carries 62 percent and 3 weeks, and names the client because the version is named (r-outcome-first-headline). Problem in two sentences, approach in three naming OpenTelemetry, gRPC batching, Redis and the flagged rollout, outcome in one sentence with the headline number; 310 words and one chart keep it on a page (r-six-slots-on-one-page). Each number is baseline, final, unit, delta and window: 560 against 1,480 is minus 62.2 percent and 14.1 against 18.4 is minus 23.4, read from server logs and a GA4 report, with the exports named under inputs_used and kept privately (r-numbers-baseline-final-delta, r-evidence-source-named-and-kept). The pull-quote is one verbatim sentence from Maria Voss, VP Engineering, Kestrel Pay, with the permission email stored beside the evidence (r-pull-quote-verbatim-with-written-permission). The client agreed to the named version, so `anonymisation` is null and the NDA indicator is named; had they declined, the anonymised block would carry the sector, size band, context and quoted role (r-nda-fallback-never-drop). One CTA to the booking page with UTM parameters, and the review is due 2026-12-08, 90 days after publication, when discovery calls attributed to the study are counted (r-single-cta-tracked-to-discovery-call).

example.title: a service-first write-up five months later
example.note: What the validator prints: `title` has no number and leads with the service (r-outcome-first-headline); `slots.problem.sentences` 4 is above 2 and `slots.approach.sentences` 1 is below 2 with an empty `stack_or_method` (r-six-slots-on-one-page); `slots.outcome.text` carries "significant" and no number (r-numbers-baseline-final-delta); the number has an empty unit, a window too short to name a period, `source_system` outside the enum and an `evidence_ref` too short (r-evidence-source-named-and-kept); the quote is "the client was very happy", the contact has no name or role and the permission was verbal (r-pull-quote-verbatim-with-written-permission); `word_count` 900 above 500 and `media_count` 3 above 1 (r-six-slots-on-one-page); `inputs_used` has 0 items where 2 are required; `cta.count` 3 and target contact_page with an untracked URL (r-single-cta-tracked-to-discovery-call). Once the schema violations are fixed the cross-field checks add: the draft is 171 days after delivery, past the 30-day cutoff; the baseline is 0; and the review is 244 days after publication, not 90.
